name: OpenFilm
cost: Free (MIT). Generated voice, music, images and video use your own keys for services like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google or fal
works_with: Codex, Claude Code or any coding agent. macOS, Windows and Linux
short: An open-source AI video agent: your coding agent writes the film as web pages, and you edit it in a local editor.
what: OpenFilm lets your coding agent make videos. The agent writes the film as one `film.html` file of tracks and clips, where each shot is a web page that draws any moment with a `frame(t)` function. Studio, a local editor in your browser, shows the film taking shape, and you can change text, layers and clips by hand or by asking.
who: People who use a coding agent and want to make launch videos, explainers or animated clips. If you don't use a coding agent, the desktop app gives you Studio with a chat beside it.
needs: Node 22.2 or later and ffmpeg (git too, for Studio's saved versions)
A Chromium-based browser such as Chrome or Edge for Studio
Optional: your own API keys for voice, music, image and video services

steps.title: Add the skills
steps.text: The first run downloads a headless Chromium of about 100 MB.

steps.title: Ask your agent for a film
steps.text: It opens the film in Studio so you can watch it come together. If your agent has no skills support, tell it to run `npx -y openfilm@latest` and follow the manual it prints.

steps.title: Or use the desktop app
steps.text: Download it for macOS or Windows from openfilm.dev or the GitHub releases. It comes with ffmpeg and the headless browser, so nothing else needs installing.

steps.title: Connect services for generated media
steps.text: Making, editing and rendering films needs no account. For generated voice, music, images and video, add your own keys in Studio under Settings → Providers.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Make a 20-second launch video for my CLI, with music.

watch: The first run downloads a headless Chromium, about 100 MB.
Generated media goes through the services you connect, with your own keys, so those services bill you.
Use a Chromium-based browser for Studio. Films are drawn and exported with that engine, so that's the preview that matches the export.
